chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Al-'Ala', who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Is one of you unable to be like the ant? For the ant drags (sustenance) to its hole.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic perspective on seeking livelihood based on the example of the ant?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the ant as a paradigm of diligent, continuous effort (*ijtihad*) in securing lawful provision, challenging believers not to be lazy despite their greater capacity. This analogy underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on combining spiritual trust in God (*tawakkul*) with active worldly endeavor, as the ant’s small scale does not excuse it from the duty of sustenance. The narration serves as a practical reminder that seeking livelihood is an act of worship when done with intention and perseverance.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Al A’ala who said,
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Is one of you frustrated that he becomes like the ant, for the ant drags (sustenance) to its hole (anthill)?’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama‘ah from those whom he has mentioned from Aban from al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘
Why should anyone among you be weaker than an ant which pulls (food) to its colony?”’
